_note: AUTHORED — never generated. How each Figma variant axis is verified against code. scripts/lib/compare-axes.mjs reads this; atlas-verify's design/figma-registry-code check enforces TOTALITY: every axis present in any atlas/metadata/<Name>.json figmaProperties must appear here, or the check FAILS. That is the ratchet — a new Figma axis cannot slip in unclassified, and an axis cannot be quietly dropped once it drifts.
milestone: M1 (docs/ATLAS-DELIVERY-ROADMAP.md). The `state` disposition is settled at M3, when the registry carries states/stateProps.

dispositions.code-union: Figma members are compared against a value list carried in atlas/metadata/<Name>.json (variants, sizes). Both directions: a member Figma has and code lacks, and a member code has and Figma lacks, both FAIL on the code side — Figma is the authority, so the fix is to add it in Figma first, re-sync, then code.
dispositions.code-connect: Figma members are compared against the keys of the corresponding figma.enum(...) in packages/figma-sync/code-connect/<Name>.figma.tsx. Both directions FAIL on the code side: Code Connect IS code. This is a real check on the code union too, not a weaker one — the figma.enum VALUES flow into the typechecked `example` closure, so `tsc` already proves they are assignable to the component's prop type. Figma -> Code Connect (here) plus Code Connect -> props (tsc) is a complete chain for axes whose value lists metadata does not carry.
dispositions.boolean: Mapped with figma.boolean(...) rather than an enum. Two-valued, so there is no member set to compare; presence of the mapping is verified, not its members.
dispositions.state: Member-level, settled by the registry (M3). A Figma State axis mixes members that map to props (disabled -> disabled, loading -> loading, error -> invalid), members that are pure CSS (hover, active, focus-visible), and a baseline (default). Code has no State union at all, and Code Connect deliberately maps only the subset that corresponds to props — so comparing member sets here would fail on every component for the wrong reason. The registry's states/stateProps settles it: design/figma-registry-code compares every member of a registered component's State axis against its entry's states, and reports the state axes of unregistered components as not yet compared. A state-like axis that is not named State (Pagination/Position) is derived from other props and has nothing to classify.
dispositions.unmapped: Figma draws this axis and nothing in code models it. Requires a reason. Reported as a WARN with the component named, never silently passing. A NEW axis is not `unmapped` by default — it is unclassified, which FAILS.
dispositions._perComponent: Any axis may carry a `components` object whose entries override the axis-level rule for one component. The same Figma axis can legitimately be treated differently per component, and an axis-level disposition alone would either flag the correctly mapped components or silently excuse the unmapped one.

Variant.reason: The primary semantic axis. metadata.variants is scraped from the exported <Name>Variant union, and 24 of the 47 Code Connect files map it as an enum, so it is checked twice over.

Size.reason: Same as Variant, via metadata.sizes and the <Name>Size union. Note Figma and code may legitimately list the same members in a different ORDER (Button: Figma sm,md,lg,xs vs code xs,sm,md,lg) — the comparator compares sets, not sequences.

State.reason: 23 components carry it. Deferred to M3 per the disposition above; this is the single largest piece of Figma-authored design information that code does not model as a union.

Orientation.reason: ButtonGroup, Divider, ScrollProgress, Slider, Stepper — all five map it as an enum.

Checked.reason: Checkbox unchecked|checked|indeterminate and Switch off|on. Checkbox's axis was renamed to Checked in Figma as the phase-2 pilot.

Placeholder.reason: DatePicker and Select empty-value rendering. Figma models it as the two-valued axis true|false, which Select maps with figma.enum and DatePicker with figma.boolean — both correct, so the comparator accepts either for a boolean axis.

Direction.reason: ListItem and RadioGroup stacking. Distinct from Orientation by component vocabulary, not by meaning — not worth unifying in Figma.

Pagination.reason: Derived state, owner decision 2026-10-23 (DEC-080, DISC-105). Figma draws Pagination/Position = start|middle|end for the first, a middle and the last page; Pagination.tsx derives it from page and pageCount and has no position prop, and none is added.

Percent.reason: Progress fill. Numeric members mapped to a value prop.

Collapsed.reason: Sidebar collapsed state as a boolean-valued enum in Figma.

Leading icon.reason: StatCard icon slot, mapped as an enum rather than a boolean.

Sparkline.reason: StatCard sparkline slot, mapped as an enum rather than a boolean.

Interaction.reason: StatCard static|hover|focus-visible|active|disabled. A second state-like axis, but unlike State it is mapped as an enum in Code Connect, so it is comparable today.

Icon only.reason: Button. Mapped with figma.boolean("Icon only") to the iconOnly prop, so there is no member set to compare.

Viewport.reason: Deliberate: Viewport (mobile|tablet|desktop) is a Figma-only presentation axis. Code derives the mobile ring from CSS and a media query rather than a prop, so there is intentionally no code prop and no Code Connect mapping. Recorded so the totality check does not flag it and so the decision is not re-litigated.

Progress.reason: Figma draws 0|50|100 as sample scroll positions. The real value is computed from scroll offset at runtime, so there is nothing to map. A presentation convenience in Figma, not a component API.

Content.reason: Figma's TableCell draws Content = text|checkbox; code composes a Checkbox into the cell instead of branching on a prop. A genuine Figma-models-more-than-code gap, left unmapped rather than inventing a prop — adding one would violate the no-new-API-on-own-initiative rule. Worth an owner decision and a DISC entry if it should be modelled.
